senses.label: Stoic attention (prosochē)
senses.summary: Constant watchfulness over one's own judgements and impulses, as a discipline of the self.
markers: attention is directed inward, at one's own judgements
hazards: Marcus's own notes practise this constantly; the word 'attention' is legitimately his.

sources.note: The Stoic discipline of attention, taught in Marcus's lifetime.

senses.label: Attention as a psychological faculty
senses.summary: Attention is studied experimentally as a limited capacity of the mind that selects among stimuli.
markers: attention is a measurable, limited capacity

sources.citation: William James, The Principles of Psychology (1890), ch. XI

senses.label: Attention as a scarce resource
senses.summary: In an information-rich world, attention is what is scarce, and products compete to capture it.
markers: attention is scarce because information is abundant
products compete for and sell people's attention

sources.citation: Herbert Simon, 'Designing organizations for an information-rich world' (1971)
sources.note: 'A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.'
